ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANYUMAS REGENCY
NUMBER 3 YEAR 2015
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF
GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
The right to a decent life, self-respect and dignity of women and children should properly receive protection in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination and the possibility of acts of violence occurring.

The policy of protection services for victims of gender-based violence and children has been normatively regulated in the Regulation of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of the Republic of Indonesia Number 01 of 2010 concerning Minimum Service Standards in the field of Integrated Services for women and children victims of violence.

Concrete steps that can be taken by the Regional Government so that women and children are protected from acts of violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and worth, can be carried out by implementing one legal rule embodied in the form of a regional regulation. The formulation of norms regarding the protection of women and children victims of violence in the form of a regional regulation needs to be carried out, the enactment of regional regulations is in order to reinforce institutional support.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims of violence, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence, community participation, implementation mechanisms, guidance, funding as well as supervision and control.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
Letter c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.
What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, aligned, and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.
Letter d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Letter e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.
Letter f What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.
What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.
Letter g What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter h What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, it is transparent among service providers.
Letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, police.
Letter j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence they experienced.
Letter k What is meant by "empowerment" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.
Letter l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.
Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

Article 13
In the Effort to Provide protection to victims of violence, the Community, Family and Parents have the obligation and responsibility: a. to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children; b. to report if violence occurs;
c. to protect victims; and
d. to provide emergency assistance.

Article 14
In implementing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government is assisted by:
a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. LPPTK.T 10

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Banyumas Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Banyumas.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a regional apparatus assigned with specific principal duties and authorities in the region.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
6. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Protection Implementation is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and services for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
13. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
14. Companion is a social worker who has professional competence in their field.

18. Article 4

Article 3

a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of households and/or communities;

6.2.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation explicitly includes trafficking victims within the protection services. b. coercion, includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

Article 14
In implementing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government is assisted by:
a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. LPPTK.T 10

Article 13
In the Effort to Provide protection to victims of violence, the Community, Family and Parents have the obligation and responsibility: a. to prevent the occurrence of violence against women and children; b. to report if violence occurs;
c. to protect victims; and
d. to provide emergency assistance.

Article 10
Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 letter e is caused by:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial;
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or sexual abuse.

6.7.rationale: The original Indonesian elucidation for Pasal 2 huruf a defines non-discrimination as protection for all victims "tanpa membedakan suku, agama, ras, golongan, ... etnis, budaya dan bahasa" (without distinguishing ethnicity/tribe, religion, race, group/class, ethnicity, culture, language, etc.). These are classic minority-group markers, so the policy explicitly commits to non-discrimination across minority characteristics. The retrieved English passage reflects this accurately. Thus, the judge’s Yes is consistent with the Indonesian ground truth, and the golden label No appears wrong (again, unless the gold standard requires special targeted measures beyond non-discrimination; the indicator as presented is about minority groups being included/recognized, which this text does).
